subject.title: [Feature]: Support sessionKey-based concurrency guard for webhook       deliveries

question: Should hook-agent deliveries with the same resolved sessionKey be rejected, skipped, queued, or remain parallel by default, and should any 409 behavior be opt-in?
rationale: The requested 409 changes an external webhook response contract and retry behavior, so automation cannot safely choose the compatibility and product policy.

options.title: Add opt-in overlap policy
options.body: Keep current accepted-by-default behavior and let trusted direct hook calls or mappings opt into reject, skip, or queue semantics with documented retry behavior.

options.title: Make 409 the default
options.body: Reject same-session active deliveries by default, accepting that existing webhook integrations may need migration to avoid retry storms.

options.title: Keep caller-managed locking
options.body: Leave OpenClaw accepting hook deliveries and document idempotency keys plus client-side locks as the supported overlap control.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in overlap policy
recommendation.body: Keep current accepted-by-default behavior and let trusted direct hook calls or mappings opt into reject, skip, or queue semantics with documented retry behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest product/security review signal for adjacent hook and session policy decisions.
